risks: Residents may fear that videos reveal poor performance; patients appear in operative videos without identifiable features.
consent: Written consent from residents for research use of their videos, separate from training; refusal has no effect on training or assessment. Patient consent to filming follows the hospital's existing policy for training videos, with no identifiable images kept.
data: Edited videos stored on an encrypted research drive, coded by resident number, deleted after rating; ratings kept without names.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: gender and seniority, because female and junior residents worry more about video use; participation and concern are reported by group only when at least five residents are in it.
effectiveness: Gives the programme a measured, if imprecise, estimate of skill gain with coaching.
efficiency: About 11 hours of rating and the coaches' existing time.
costs: No new costs beyond editing time.
grants: None needed; a surgical education grant could fund a multi-programme study later.
partnerships: Programme director, two consultant coaches, two resident representatives.
rebPath: Research ethics board review of a study with residents as participants under ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki; decision not yet sought.
summary: Minimal-risk study whose main ethical issue is protecting residents from use of videos in assessment.
